scope: Both multipart families:24 questions/72 numeric rubric parts. First substantive self-review; not an official AP rubric, independent review or empirically validated polytomous scale.

entries.reasoning: Equating a-Q=20+Q gives Q0=(a-20)/2. After the seller tax, buyer willingness to pay equals20+Q+t, so Qt=(a-20-t)/2. Across n=0..11, Qt=26+n>0 and Qt<Q0; both equilibria are interior. Revenue=tQt, not tQ0. Linear upward supply and downward demand support the wedge and lost-trade explanation; no externalities are specified. All three parts use the same economic scenario and are locally dependent.
entries.rubric: Three equal one-point numeric parts. A correct revenue answer receives its point even if another part is wrong; revenue calculated from an incorrect submitted quantity receives no point unless it independently equals the key. No work, justification or error-carried-forward scoring.
entries.numericVerification: All12 variants independently verified from displayed prompt values; every one-part error and selected carried-forward errors tested against the actual scorer.
entries.measurement: Score is formative normalized rubric credit. Parts must not be treated as independent binary IRT observations; multipart items currently excluded from binary calibration.

entries.reasoning: Demand P=a-2Q implies MR=a-4Q as stated. MR=20 gives Qm=(a-20)/4; demand gives Pm=(a+20)/2. The efficient marginal condition P=MC gives Qc=(a-20)/2=2Qm. Lost surplus is0.5(Qc-Qm)(Pm-20), positive throughout n=0..11. Marginal profit decreases strictly, and explicit operation/no-capacity assumptions exclude shutdown and capacity corners. No externalities permits the standard marginal-surplus welfare comparison.
entries.rubric: Three equal one-point numeric parts. Price and deadweight loss must match their correct values; mechanically consistent follow-on values from an incorrect quantity do not earn credit. This is numeric partial credit, not a complete AP free-response rubric.
